method: Read-only. Loaded docs/work-inventory.json (35.7MB, all 38 corpus books, live at current HEAD) and imported scripts/completion_atlas.py's pure `_bucket_of`/`partition` functions in-process (verified no I/O, guarded by `if __name__=='__main__'`) to bucket-classify every unit without running any regenerator. Grouped non-DONE units by `evidence` with everything after the first ':' stripped (C1.5's stated method) to reproduce the mechanism census. Cross-checked candidate engines against src/rules_core source (formula_interpreter.rs, bonus_stack_reader.rs, race_trait_formula_binding.rs, simple_kind_tables.rs) and docs/retro/*.md for build-cost calibration.

critical_finding_state_drift.summary: forward-plan.json's own figures (generated_at_head fef202a5, dated 2026-08-27 per its C metadata) are stale relative to the live corpus at current HEAD (2026-08-31, 4 days / waves 20-22 later). The 35-book (non-vehicle) non-DONE population dropped from 29,283 to 22,369 in that window, driven almost entirely by bucket V collapsing from 6,747 to 175 -- the SD-33 oracle harness clearing thousands of units corpus-wide since the snapshot. B (11,299) and C (3,981) are UNCHANGED; only V and M moved.
critical_finding_state_drift.provenance: MEASURED (re-partitioned live units via completion_atlas._bucket_of, n=42,472 total / 22,369 non-DONE, this session, HEAD b4485ae5) vs MEASURED (forward-plan.json's own stated n=29,283, HEAD fef202a5, 2026-08-27)
critical_finding_state_drift.implication: The oracle harness is not a projected lever -- it is the single mechanism that has ALREADY delivered the largest realized ROI in this program's recent history (thousands of V units cleared in ~4 days across many books at once, not one book at a time). Any SD-35 costing built on forward-plan.json's bucket totals without re-deriving live will overstate remaining V work by ~38x and understate how much of the 'UNPRICED 45.7%' figure has already shrunk.

mechanism_census.reproduction_note: Could not reproduce forward-scope-register.md C1.5's exact '136 distinct mechanisms / 35,650 of 49,438' figures by the stated method at either the 2026-08-27 snapshot or live HEAD -- got 180 mechanisms / 49,438-total-population at a same-vintage re-derivation attempt, and 94 mechanisms / 24,475 non-DONE at live HEAD. C1.5 itself is dated 2026-08-27 and the corpus has moved since (see drift finding above), and no committed script implements the exact grouping (grepped scripts/ and docs/ for the method; none found), so exact reconciliation of the integer 136 is a measurement gap, not a fabricated match. The QUALITATIVE finding -- a small number of generic mechanisms dominate the non-DONE population -- reproduces cleanly: live HEAD shows the top 25 of 94 mechanisms cover 90.2% of the 24,475-unit non-DONE population (all 38 books).

gaps: Could not reproduce forward-scope-register.md C1.5's exact 136-mechanism / 35,650-unit / 29-mechanism-covers-90% figures -- no committed script implements the stated grouping method, and the corpus has moved since C1.5's 2026-08-27 vintage. Reported a live re-derivation (94 mechanisms / 24,475 non-DONE, top 25 cover 90.2%) instead, flagged as a different but comparable measurement.

The oracle_probe_surface_for_no_table_kinds capability (2,062 units, bucket V) appears to conflict with decisions.md §19's own disposition rule (status=='oracle-unverifiable' maps to DONE) -- unresolved whether this population is still open work or already dispositioned; not confident enough to rank it.

Bucket M's true rate is unmeasured corpus-wide (forward-plan.json measured_rates.M is null); rank 3's ROI is an extrapolation from a different engine's widening history (SD-32 formula_interpreter/bonus_stack_reader T12), not this population's own data.

Whether each M-bucket mechanism's magnitude is actually formula/bonus-shaped (and therefore reachable by the existing engines at all, vs needing bespoke per-kind compute) was not verified record-by-record -- assumed plausible from the engine's stated scope, not confirmed.
